scope.method: Triaged the original repositories; read substantive documents, selected implementation files, author histories, release records, papers, original essays, and publisher metadata for the included work. Stars informed triage but did not establish completion or contribution.
scope.limits: This is a curated public-work audit, not a claim to have read every file in all 214 repositories or to have found every article and appearance. Medium archive requests were unavailable; individual public articles were verified. Commit histories capped at 100 were not treated as complete contribution counts.
scope.video_method: Read the complete public uploads catalog through normal public playlist continuation, six official podcast playlists, and individual player metadata, descriptions and chapters for the selected full recordings. Checked the oldest upload directly, including its Hungarian title, expanded description, and publication date. Did not watch or transcribe every upload; clips were not counted as full interviews.

entries.title: Longevity World Cup
entries.description: I created and host a competition to reverse biological aging. Participants compete on biological-age estimates from blood tests. I began building it in 2024, ran a public beta, and formally launched it on 16 September 2025.
entries.inspected: First-person About and history, source history, launch and beta essays, live competition.

entries.title: Immortal Combat
entries.description: A podcast I’ve hosted since 2024. I talk with researchers and people working to extend healthy life.
entries.inspected: Official channel and playlist, individual episode descriptions and publication metadata; user selected Annie as the first recommendation.

entries.title: zkSNACKs
entries.description: I co-founded the company in 2018 with Bálint Harmat and Gergely Hajdu to develop Wasabi Wallet. I served as its early CTO, built the technical team, and later led research. By 2020, I had handed over the CTO and code-maintainer responsibilities to concentrate on the next generation of Bitcoin privacy. The company had grown to 30 full-time contributors when I left in December 2023.
entries.inspected: Read the 2018 talk, leadership-handover issue and December 2023 farewell; Forbes confirms co-founder and research-leader roles.

entries.title: Wasabi Wallet
entries.description: I created the Bitcoin privacy wallet, following my earlier HiddenWallet work, and led its early development. It brought CoinJoin, Tor, and private transaction discovery into one wallet. Version 1.0 was released on 31 October 2018; the second generation, released in June 2022, uses WabiSabi for CoinJoins with different amounts.
entries.inspected: Original release, first-person wallet history, contemporary Anonymous Bitcoin and network-privacy essays, 2.0 launch account.

after.label: Forbes Hungary included me in its 2020 30 Under 30 list for this work.

entries.title: ZeroLink: The Bitcoin Fungibility Framework
entries.description: I created ZeroLink in 2017. It combines Chaumian CoinJoin with requirements for coin selection, transaction fees, and how a wallet treats coins before and after mixing. Those surrounding rules matter because a private mixing round can still be undone by later wallet behavior.
entries.inspected: Independent full-Git genesis audit and original framework; user attribution correction is authoritative.

entries.title: TumbleBit / NTumbleBit
entries.description: Nicolas Dorier and I worked on an independent implementation in 2016–2017. My contributions included wallet integration, Tor support, configuration, and documentation. The original NDSS paper names us as implementers and thanks me for discussions and suggestions. I wrote a five-part series explaining the protocol and how to try the implementation.
entries.inspected: Paper pages 3 and 14, NTumbleBit author history and tree, all five article links. Implementation and acknowledgment, not paper authorship.

entries.title: WabiSabi: Centrally Coordinated CoinJoins with Variable Amounts
entries.description: I co-authored the paper with István András Seres, Yuval Kogman, and Lucas Ontivero. Anonymous credentials let participants register outputs of different amounts without revealing to the coordinator which inputs paid for them. Value commitments enforce the accounting. This is the protocol used in Wasabi 2.0.
entries.inspected: Journal author order and publication record, preprint, protocol document. Preprint and journal publication are one work.

entries.title: Pay To EndPoint (P2EP)
entries.description: I co-proposed P2EP after a group discussion and published its explanation in July 2018. Sender and receiver both contribute inputs to a payment, disrupting the assumption that all inputs belong to the sender. Nicolas Dorier’s later BIP78 Payjoin proposal acknowledges my implementation feedback.
entries.inspected: Original design article and BIP78 acknowledgment. No sole-inventor or BIP-author claim.

entries.title: Wasabi Research Club / Wasabi Research Experience
entries.description: I helped start these public discussions of Bitcoin privacy research in 2020. We reviewed existing protocols and invited their authors before moving on to our own WabiSabi research. The archive includes meeting agendas, notes, slides, and recordings on CoinShuffle, SNICKER, CashFusion, anonymous credentials, and WabiSabi.
entries.inspected: Repository genesis and 65-author-commit history, README and agendas, club transcript, first-person Wasabigeddon account. No assertion that the club ended in 2021 or that Adam presented every meeting.

entries.title: Dumplings and CoinJoin analysis
entries.description: I built Dumplings in 2020 to derive reproducible CoinJoin statistics from Bitcoin blockchain data. It separates newly mixed coins from remixes and examines change and post-mix consolidation. This follows my earlier CoinJoin-efficiency and Wasabi-versus-Whirlpool analyses. The academic study Adoption and Actual Privacy of Decentralized CoinJoin Implementations in Bitcoin builds on and evaluates these detection heuristics.
entries.inspected: Scanner, Statista, Analysis, command handling, READMEs and authored history; read the academic paper’s methodology and software citations. Detection heuristics are not exact user counts. Adam is not an author of the cited study.

entries.title: CoinJoin amount design / Sake
entries.description: Allowing different input amounts creates a practical question: how should those amounts be split into outputs? I wrote amount-organization simulations in 2020 and began Sake in December 2021, with later contributions from the team. It compares denomination strategies, equal outputs, change, fees, and block-space use. Dumplings supplies parameters from real transactions; my Wasabi 2.0 launch log compares the simulations with mainnet output decompositions.
entries.inspected: Sake denomination, mixer, analyzer and results code; first and later author history; earlier AmountOrganization branch; launch-log comparison. Sake has substantive work despite low stars. Do not claim exclusive authorship of team algorithms.

entries.title: CoinShuffle++ review
entries.description: My 2018 technical review of the protocol, organized as questions, answers, and unresolved points.
entries.inspected: Read the full substantive Q&A document and review history. A review, not protocol co-authorship.

entries.title: ShareLock: Mixing for Cryptocurrencies from Multiparty ECDSA
entries.description: Omer Shlomovits and István András Seres thank me for insightful discussions in their 2019 paper.
entries.inspected: Original abstract and acknowledgment. Acknowledged discussion, not paper authorship.

entries.title: DotNetWallet / HiddenWallet
entries.description: I wrote a cross-platform command-line wallet for the 2016 tutorial Build a Bitcoin wallet in C#. It covered wallet creation and recovery, receiving, balance and transaction history, and sending. That work developed into HiddenWallet, the precursor to Wasabi. I also contributed to the early Breeze TumbleBit wallet in 2017.
entries.inspected: Full tutorial README, CLI Program implementation and 55-author-commit history; 34 Breeze author commits and contemporary first-person account. Full-node mode in DotNetWallet was explicitly unimplemented; not promoted as a feature.

entries.title: HiddenBitcoin / HBitcoin
entries.description: My privacy-oriented Bitcoin libraries built on Nicolas Dorier’s NBitcoin. They supported wallet and transaction handling, including full-block SPV wallet work. These are part of the history leading to HiddenWallet and Wasabi.
entries.inspected: Full READMEs, HBitcoin wallet-job implementation and author histories; acknowledge underlying NBitcoin.

entries.title: DotNetTor
entries.description: I built this .NET Core library for sending HTTP traffic through Tor’s SOCKS interface and managing Tor circuits. It supported my wallet and NTumbleBit work.
entries.inspected: README, SOCKS HTTP handler and control client source, NuGet publication and authored history; not an invention of Tor.

entries.title: Wallet network privacy
entries.description: I investigated how a lightweight wallet can discover its transactions without telling a server which addresses it owns. My writing examines full-block downloads, client-side filtering, Tor, and their privacy tradeoffs.
entries.inspected: Read original articles and ClientSideFilteringMinusMinus proposal. Context for actual wallet work, not an invented Neutrino/BIP157/BIP158 authorship claim or a standalone promotion of a zero-star sketch.

entries.title: Programming the Blockchain in C#
entries.description: Originally written by Nicolas Dorier, with Bill Strait and me credited as co-authors. I updated and extended explanations for the second community edition and brought the book into GitHub for community development.
entries.inspected: Read cover, foreword, second-edition foreword, authored edits and full-Git history from May 2016.

entries.title: BitcoinGenie
entries.description: Code accompanying my 2016 tutorial on constructing Bitcoin transactions in C#. It walks through the transaction’s inputs and outputs, signing, and the serialized result.
entries.inspected: Read the README and complete interactive Program source. Tutorial, not a production wallet.

entries.title: Rating Bitcoin Wallets
entries.description: A 2018 comparison framework expanding Jonas Schnelli’s wallet triangle. It examines privacy, trust, security, and usability in the wallets available at the time.
entries.inspected: Read the complete framework and creation history. Historical framework, not current wallet recommendations.

entries.title: Forever Alone Programming
entries.description: My adaptation of the Agile Unified Process for solo programmers and small teams. Its four phases cover choosing an idea, checking feasibility, prototyping, construction, release, and maintenance.
entries.inspected: Read overview and all four phase documents; substantive published methodology, unlike EDD.

entries.title: ClipboardButler
entries.description: A Windows utility that cleans tracking parameters and redirect wrappers from copied links. It runs in the system tray and applies rules for supported sites, including YouTube, X, Google, Facebook, Instagram, and Amazon.
entries.inspected: Read README, tray Program, clipboard manager, text-cleaning rules and tests. No universal claim to remove every tracker.

entries.title: Nomadic Method
entries.description: A workout app that adapts a session to the time available.
entries.inspected: Live usable app and source; user wants it retained as a smaller project, below principal company and longevity work.

entries.title: Pursuit of Value with Derek Mazzone
entries.description: My 2023 conversation series with Derek Mazzone, author of The Pursuit of Value: A Philosophy of Loss and Equanimity. Across eight recordings, we discuss method, value, religion, ethics, meaning, and mind.
entries.inspected: Official eight-recording playlist; full video titles, dates, descriptions and chapters. Adam is the conversation host, not author of Derek’s book.

entries.description: I co-hosted this Bitcoin news and technology podcast.
entries.inspected: User confirms co-host role; official channel episode #172 explicitly credits Nopara alongside Shinobius, Janine and Rick. Removed unrelated Medium-publication credit.

entries.inspected: Official full video, description and publication date; a conversation predating Immortal Combat.

entries.inspected: Original grants announcement lists review committee. Do not imply a personal grant award.
